measured.how: The page's Measure speed button gave these rates on 5 October 2026 in headless Chromium: about 1.9 million replicates a second with 4 workers for the Poisson experiment, and about 62,000 for the survey workflow with 1,000 draws in each replicate. With the main thread 4 times slower, as on an ordinary laptop, the main thread alone gives 211,000 and 4,300. Thus a run of 2^22 replicates of a light model takes about 10 s on an ordinary laptop, and the time limit pauses a longer run. On 6 October 2026 the same button measured the group 3 models: about 1.1 million replicates a second with the workers for a Pareto experiment, and about 105,000 for the slowest workflow, a censored trial with 100 patients and Kaplan–Meier estimates in each replicate (7,600 on the slowed main thread). Its default size of 2^13 thus takes about 1 s on an ordinary laptop, so the published limits hold.
